P-07-shest-otrasley.текст: A single ultra-premium cinematic frame in 16:9 landscape at 1920 by 1080 pixels, composed like the cover of a serious business magazine and never like a presentation slide: a monumental Moscow production building is sliced open frontally into an architectural cutaway that reveals six deep working bays arranged as a strict honeycomb of rectangular cells, two rows by three columns, every cell a genuine interior with cast concrete walls, riveted steel columns, an overhead crane rail, a polished sealed floor carrying honest scuffs, and a shallow pool of warm light on the ground. Reading the top row left to right and then the bottom row left to right, the six bays hold: a metalworking shop with a lathe, a press brake and coiled sheet steel; a joinery with a panel saw, stacked boards and clamped frames; a print shop with a sheet-fed press and pallets of paper; an electronics room with clean benches, component trays and antistatic mats; a food production room with stainless tanks, extraction hoods and tiled surfaces; a building-materials bay with a mixer, stacked pallets and bagged goods. The bays are empty of people so that architecture and numerals carry the frame. The infographic is physically built into the scene rather than pasted on top: the cut edge of every concrete slab is faced with a brushed steel plate bolted with four visible hex bolts, and each industry caption is deep-engraved into that steel with a fine machined groove that catches the key light, while a thin hairline leader rule, one pixel to two pixels thick, runs from each plate horizontally into its bay and terminates in a small filled square tick, never crossing another leader. A sheet of semi-transparent tracing paper is laid physically over the left third of the frame, its edge slightly curled and weighted by a flat steel bar, and the headline is printed on that tracing sheet in dense condensed technical sans with wide letter tracking, so that the concrete texture reads faintly through the paper fibre. The exact inscription «100 ПРОИЗВОДСТВ» sits in the upper left of the frame on a single line with no hyphenation, its capital height about twelve percent of the frame height and the numeral 100 the single largest element in the whole image, dominant over every machine and every beam. Directly beneath it, sharing the same left margin and left alignment, the exact line «1000 человек на одной территории» runs as one unbroken line at a capital height of about two and a half percent of the frame height, separated from the headline by a clear gap equal to one headline capital height and underlined by a single hairline rule. The six engraved steel captions read exactly «Металлообработка», «Мебель», «Полиграфия», «Электроника», «Пищевое», «Стройматериалы», each one placed at the lower left corner of its own bay, all six at a capital height of about one and eight tenths percent of the frame height, the three captions of a row sharing one perfect baseline and the two rows sharing one vertical rhythm. Geometry is strict and measured: a twelve column grid with five percent outer margins, the honeycomb of bays aligned to columns four through twelve, every caption plate inset by exactly one grid gutter from its bay edge, a guaranteed clear space of at least two and a half percent of the frame height around every piece of type so that nothing collides, overlaps, touches a column or is clipped by the frame. The palette is locked to five hexadecimal values and nothing else exists anywhere in the picture, including reflections, glints, rust, skin, product colour and spill light: amber #E8A400 as the one and only accent, used for the light source, the leader ticks and the engraved grooves; muted gold #C9A233 for secondary reflections on steel and brass; graphite #14171C for dense concrete and machine bodies; ink black #0E1116 for the surrounding void, the deep shadows and the background; warm white #F5F1E8 for lit planes, hairline rules and all type. No blue, no green, no red, no cyan, no magenta, no teal, no neon, no cyberpunk glow, no colour grading outside these five values. Lighting is architectural and cinematic: a single hard directional amber key enters from the upper right at roughly thirty five degrees, rakes across the concrete cut edges and grazes the engraved lettering so the grooves throw micro shadows, a very weak warm white bounce lifts the lower left, shadows fall long, deep and soft-edged with visible volumetric falloff into black, and a faint haze of dust hangs in the amber beam. P-13-chetyre-bloka.текст: A single ultra-premium cinematic frame in 16:9 landscape at 1920 by 1080 pixels, built like the cover of a business quarterly and not like a slide: a precise axonometric cutaway, thirty degree isometric projection with no perspective distortion, of four industrial blocks standing side by side on a dark polished ground plane, each block a real building volume with concrete walls, exposed steel portal frames, a roof partly cut away to show the interior, and its own sectional roll-up loading gate on the front face with a rubber bumper, a bollard and a shallow ramp.
